t: Year-End Planning: Capital Gains Distributions | Wealthspire
s: November 26, 2024 - Tax-inefficient investments, such as high-income bond funds and actively managed equity funds, could be held in tax-deferred accounts like IRAs and 401(k)s. Bond funds generate interest income that is taxed at ordinary rates, and actively managed funds typically have higher turnover, leading to more taxable capital gains. Tax-efficient investments, including passive equity funds and municipal bond funds, could be held in taxable accounts. Passive equities usually have lower turnover, leading to fewer taxable capital gains distributions, and municipal bonds (in most cases) pay interest income that is exempt from federal income tax, as they are issued by state and local governments.
